 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08-04-2022 at about 7.15 p.m., in front of Manjunatha House,
Goramadagu-Kothanur road, Goramadagu village, Chikkaballapur district, when the petitioner was pedestrian, walking slowly, carefully and cautiously on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 rode his vehicle in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, in high speed without observing any traffic rules and dashed to the petitioner from behind.
As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner was thrown out, fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Rajesh Hospital, Chintamani, wherein she took first aid treatment and thereafter, she was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar,
wherein she took further treatment as an indoor patient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was doing agriculture and milk vending and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has became permanently disabled and lost her earning capacity.
The Shidlaghatta Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two-wheeler for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 remained absent.

Hence, placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03/EK-1914 in the alleged accident.
It has further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner.
The injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner are also denied.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.

Further,
it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, alleged to have occurred on 08-04-2022, at about 7.15 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-03/EK-1914 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6 . In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got herself examined as PW-1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.
Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Imran Hussain S/o Ahamed Hussain as P.W.2 and closed her side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 is placed ex-parte.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 08-04-2022 at about 7.15 p.m., in front of Manjunatha House, Goramadagu-Kothanur road, Goramadagu Village, Chikkaballapur district,
when she was walking slowly, carefully and cautiously on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 rode his vehicle in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, in high speed without observing any traffic rules and dashed her from behind.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has became permanently disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., and first information statement, Ex.P.2 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Seizure Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is discharge summary, Ex.P.8 are medical bills (total 17), Ex.P.9 are prescriptions (total 9), Ex.P.10 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.11 are X-ray (total six), Ex.P.12 is Clinical Examination Note,
Ex.P.13 is Disability Evaluation Form, Ex.P.14 is IP record and Ex.P.15 is the x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, on 08-04- 2022 at about 7.15 p.m., in front of Manjunatha House, Goramadagu-Kothanur road, Goramadagu Village, Chikkaballapur district, the petitioner was pedestrian and when she was walking on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 has dashed her from behind.
As a result of the forced impact, she sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.
The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03/EK-1914 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.

Further, the Ex.P.2 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the petitioner was walking on the left side of the 12 feet width road and the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 dashed her from behind.

12. The petitioner, who is examined as P.W.1, has deposed in her examination-in-chief affidavit that,
on 08-04- 2022 at about 7.15 p.m., in front of Manjunatha House, Goramadagu-Kothanur road,
Goramadagu Village, Chikkaballapur district, when she was walking on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 came in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to her from behind.
As a result of the forced impact, she sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.
The said facts have remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, though the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and in the cross-examination of P.W.1., it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 03/EK-1914.
Further, she has clearly denied the suggestion that, the said accident has occurred due to her own negligence.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 X-ray films, Ex.P.12 Clinical Examination Note and Ex.P.13 Disability Evaluation Form, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, on 08/04/2022, the petitioner was brought to Gaurav Hospital, at Kolar, with the history of road traffic accident and on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner had fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.6, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03/EK-1914.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-EK-1914 and she has sustained fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg and for the said injuries she has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 21-09-1970.
The accident has taken place on 08/04/2022 at about 7:15 P.M. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 52 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 36% physical disability of left lower limb and for the whole body he has 12% physical disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 X-ray films, Ex.P.12 Clinical Examination Note and Ex.P.13 Disability Evaluation Form clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made in to him that, the Ex.P.12 to 14 documents are not related to the petitioner, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 08-04-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 07-11-2023, which is after lapse of one and half year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of the implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.

As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion Bhagyamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64636766/
6 of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fractures on the left leg of the petitioner are united with implants in situ.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was doing agriculture and milk vending and was earning income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do agriculture work and milk vending.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was doing agriculture and milk vending.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 52 years is 11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 10/100 X 11 = Rs.2,04,600/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 17 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.69,887/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.69,887/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her left leg i.e. suffered fracture of tibia and fibula of her left leg.

As per Ex.P.12 Clinical Examination Note and Ex.P.14 In-Patient Record, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 08-04-2022 to 11-04-2022, in Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar.
She has also underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.
Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.14 In-Patient Record, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 08-04-2022 to 11-04-2022, in Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar.

She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that Bhagyamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64636766/
7 period.

entities.text: Bhagyamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd

sentences.text: Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 4 = Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.14 In- Patient Record, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 08-04-2022 to 11-04-2022, in Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 4 = Rs.3,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Goramadagu village, Shidlaghatta taluka,
Chikkaballapur District, the accident has taken place at Goramadagu village, Chikkaballapur district and she has taken treatment at Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient at Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 52 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones i.e. tibia and fibula of her left leg.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which costs about Rs.35,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
The cost of surgery for removal of implants quoted by P.W.2 seems exaggerated.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
19.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,04,600-00 2.
Medical expenses 69,887-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 4,000-00 5.

8 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03/EK-1914 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- (Rupees three lakhs ninety six thousand six hundred and eighty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08-04-2022 at about 7.15 p.m., in front of Manjunatha House,
Goramadagu-Kothanur road, Goramadagu village, Chikkaballapur district, when the petitioner was pedestrian, walking slowly, carefully and cautiously on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 rode his vehicle in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, in high speed without observing any traffic rules and dashed to the petitioner from behind.
opennyai_summary.facts:
As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner was thrown out, fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.
The Shidlaghatta Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two-wheeler for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, alleged to have occurred on 08-04-2022, at about 7.15 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-03/EK-1914 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 03/EK-1914.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03/EK-1914 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.6, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03/EK-1914.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion Bhagyamma vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64636766/
6 of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was doing agriculture and milk vending.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00
Total Rs. 3,96,687-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,96,687/- (Rupees three lakhs ninety six thousand six hundred and eighty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
